previous_assumption: assumed useState(Boolean(someQueryParam)) was a safe way to open a dialog or expand a row based on a query param present at load time
correction: It only runs once, at first mount -- router.push to the same route with only the query string changed (exactly what a notification bell click does) does not remount the page in the App Router, it only re-renders with new searchParams, so the initializer never re-fires and the derived state silently stays at its original value regardless of what the URL now says. QuotationsPage's createOpen (gating CreateQuotationDialog) had this bug -- confirmed correct by contrast with quotationIdParam's redirect two lines below it, already correctly implemented as a useEffect keyed on the param. Fixed by adding the matching effect. Caught the identical bug in my own very recent commit before it was reported: billing/page.tsx's InvoiceRow had the same useState(Boolean(highlighted)) for its expanded state -- the ?invoiceId= deep link's data fetch worked (that part was already a reactive effect) but the row never actually expanded to show it. Fixed by moving setExpanded(true) into the existing effect instead of the initializer. Same pattern (useState seeded from searchParams.get(...) or a derived boolean from one) also exists for tab state in settings/page.tsx, machines/[id]/page.tsx, and rentals/[id]/page.tsx -- plausibly the same bug when navigating to those via a Link while the page is already mounted in a different tab, but left unverified/unfixed since unreported -- worth checking if a similar link-doesn't-do-what-it-says report comes in for those. General lesson: any useState initializer derived from useSearchParams() on a page that can be reached via client-side query-only navigation (not just a fresh hard load) needs a companion useEffect, not just the initializer, or it silently goes stale.
